items.title: NEW — `_` as the ANONYMOUS TYPE BINDER: `impl Source<Option<_: Source<type U>>>` for today's `type _: Source<type U>` — the pattern wildcard's spelling (`Some(_)`, `let _`) in the impl-subject position. Today `_` in a type position is refused 'cannot find type `_`' and `_: Bound` is a parse error at the `:` (only the `type` keyword reaches `parse_type_binder`, parsing.rs:4430/4495), while `type _` and `type _: Bound` both compile — so the anonymous binder exists and only its spelling is heavy
items.discussion: the owner's ask (2026-09-11) with the exhibit `impl Source<Option<type _: Source<type U>>> { fun foo(self) .. }` over `Signal::new(Some(Signal::new(0)))` — compiles as written (probe), the `_:` form does not; Order 32 lane smalls-32
items.body:
**Today.** `parse_type_atom` (parsing.rs:4430) routes the `type` keyword to `parse_type_binder` (:4495: `type NAME (: A + B)?` → `Node::TypeBinder(name, bounds)`), and nothing else in a type position may carry a bound. `_` is an ordinary identifier there, so `impl Source<Option<_>>` fails name resolution ('cannot find type `_`') and `impl Source<Option<_: Source<type U>>>` fails to parse at the `:` ("found ':' expected ',' or '>'", then a cascaded '`Option` takes 1 type argument, 0 given'). `impl Source<Option<type _>>` and `impl Source<Option<type _: Source<type U>>>` both compile — the anonymous binder is already a thing, spelled with the keyword.

**The change.** In `parse_type_atom`, an `_` identifier in type position, optionally followed by `: bounds`, parses as the SAME `Node::TypeBinder("_", bounds)` the keyword form produces — one node, one analyzer path, no new semantics. `type _` stays accepted (the formatter canonicalises it to `_` — or the other way; pick the wildcard, it is what the owner asked for and what `Some(_)` reads as). A NAMED binder keeps its keyword (`type U` — the keyword is what says 'this introduces a name' in a position that otherwise reads a type).

**Check before building (a pin either way):** what two anonymous binders in one head mean today — `impl Pair<type _, type _>` — are they ONE parameter named `_` (an aliasing bug the wildcard must not inherit) or two fresh ones? `Some(_, _)` binds nothing twice; the type form must be fresh each time. Also: a bare `_` OUTSIDE an impl head (`let x: List<_> = ..`, an inference placeholder in an annotation) is a DIFFERENT feature — out of scope here; the refusal it gets today ('cannot find type `_`') should instead say what `_` is for after this lands (a curated message, one row).

**Estate.** spec/grammar.md:249 and spec/types.md:318 document the keyword form — add the wildcard beside it; the EBNF gate (`grammar_ebnf`); `vilan fmt` prints the chosen canonical form (a formatter pin); the TextMate grammar needs nothing (`_` is not a keyword; E161 is the highlighting item for these heads). Pins: the owner's exhibit with `_:`; the two-wildcards-fresh pin; `type _` still accepted; the `let` placeholder refusal text.

items.title: NEW — `flatten` is INHERENT on `SignalCell<SignalCell<U>>` (reactive.vl:890) while the read contract is the `Source` TRAIT: a source whose element is itself a source — a `map` result, a derived cell, a `SignalCell<Option<SignalCell<T>>>`, the owner's `Source<Option<type _: Source<type U>>>` — has no `flatten`. Make it a BLANKET over the trait (`impl Source<type I: Source<type U>> { fun flatten(self): SignalCell<U> }` — the bare-trait impl subject compiles today, probed) plus the `Option` form (`Source<Option<I>>` → `SignalCell<Option<U>>`), and CENSUS the other inherent blocks on concrete reactive types for members that are trait-shaped: `RemoteSource::{or, status}` (rpc.vl:2937) and `KeyedSource::{or, status, of}` (:3596) each re-implement `or` over `Source<Option<T>>`; `SignalCell::update` (inherent by A32's ruling), `Draft`, `Selector`, `Optimistic` stay
items.discussion: the owner's ask (2026-09-11): 'make the flatten method in std trait based instead of `SignalCell` struct, and any other impls that should be trait based'; Order 32 lane reactive-32 (it owns reactive.vl); B275 (supertrait argument threading, solver-32) is the one solver gap a nested-bound blanket could hit — probe first
items.body:
**Today.** `Source<T>` (reactive.vl:482) carries the derivation defaults — `sub`, `effect`, `map` (:546, returning `SignalCell<U>`) — so every source derives. `flatten` (the monadic join, A4) is the exception: `impl SignalCell<SignalCell<type U>> { fun flatten(self): SignalCell<U> }` at :890, inherent on the CELL, so `outer.map(..).flatten()` over a derived outer, or a `SignalCell<Option<SignalCell<T>>>` (the owner's shape: an optional inner signal), has nothing to call. `MaybeSignal` (:740) shows the trait-shaped form beside it: `impl type S: Source<type T> with MaybeSignal<T>`.

**The change.** (1) `impl Source<type I: Source<type U>> { fun flatten(self): SignalCell<U> }` — the body is the shipped one (outer `sub` registered with the owner, a rolling inner subscription deferred to the owner, A28's ownership story unchanged); the `SignalCell<SignalCell<U>>` impl goes (the blanket covers it — pin that the existing flatten pins stay green as the control). (2) The `Option` form: `impl Source<Option<type I: Source<type U>>> { fun flatten(self): SignalCell<Option<U>> }` — `None` outer → `None`, a `Some(inner)` follows the inner; the owner's probe `impl Source<Option<type _: Source<type U>>>` is this impl's head and compiles at 65af4be0. A default method on `Source<T>` cannot express either (a default cannot add a bound on `T`), so the blanket is the honest spelling — say so in the doc comment. (3) Census: `RemoteSource::or` (rpc.vl:2943) and `KeyedSource::or` (:3636) are two copies of 'a `Source<Option<T>>` with a seed' → one `impl Source<Option<type T>> { fun or(self, initial: T): SignalCell<T> }` in reactive.vl (both mirrors implement `Source<Option<..>>`, :2856/:3529); `status()` stays on the mirrors (it reads mirror state a plain source has none of); `KeyedSource::of(key)` stays keyed. Report every other inherent member you judged and why it stayed.

**Risk.** Impl selection over a bound whose ARGUMENT is itself bounded (`I: Source<U>` inside `Source<I>`) is B268's machinery with B275's supertrait gap beside it — probe the blanket against `SignalCell<SignalCell<i32>>`, a `map` result, and `SignalCell<Option<SignalCell<i32>>>` BEFORE moving anything; if the selector cannot see through, the finding goes to solver-32's territory as an OPEN Q and the inherent impl stays. Pins (`reactive_lifetimes.rs` beside the A4 pins): flatten over a `map` result; the Option form's `None`/`Some`/switch; the ownership pin (a replaced inner stops driving) re-run through the blanket; `or` over both mirrors unchanged (the channel pins are the control). Docs: std/reactive.md's `flatten` paragraph.

items.title: NEW — the TextMate grammar mis-scopes a nested generic head: in `impl Source<Option<type _: Source<type U>>>` the `type` binder keyword is `storage.type.vilan` (the declaration-keyword scope — `fun`/`struct`/`impl` — which most themes colour like a type name), `<type` matches the ELEMENT rule (vilan.tmLanguage.json:388: a lowercase name glued to `<` is a tag, so that bracket is `punctuation.definition.tag.vilan`), the other angle brackets fall to the bare-operator fallback (`keyword.operator.vilan`, :380), and a line-leading `>` is E115's multi-line element terminator (`punctuation.definition.tag.vilan`) — three scopes for one bracket kind and a keyword coloured as a type
items.discussion: the owner's report (2026-09-11) on the large-type heads B294/A86 write; the scopes named are TextMate's, so it is the grammar first — but vilan-lsp ALSO emits semantic tokens (main.rs:251 `encode_semantic_tokens`, E2's classified spans), and in VS Code the semantic layer overrides TextMate where it classifies, so the lane confirms which layer painted each colour (`vilan.semanticTokens.enabled` off, compare); Order 32 lane smalls-32
items.body:
**Mechanism, read from the grammar at 65af4be0.** (1) `type` sits in the declaration-keyword list (`storage.type.vilan`: `fun|struct|enum|impl|trait|type|mod|macro`, :303) — right for `type Alias = ..`, wrong for the BINDER inside a head, where it introduces a parameter. (2) The element rule (:388, `(</?)([a-z][a-zA-Z0-9_]*(?:-[a-zA-Z0-9_]+)*)\\s*(/?>)?`) fires on `<type`, `<sync`, `<str` — any lowercase word glued to `<` — so `Option<type _` opens a 'tag' named `type`. (3) Every other `<`/`>` in a type is the operator fallback's single-character class (:380, `[-+*/=<>!&|^?%]`). (4) A wrapped head whose continuation line starts with `>` (or `>>>`) hits the E115 terminator rule (`^\\s*(/?>)`), scoped as a tag delimiter.

**Fix (TextMate, line-based and regex-only, so structure by begin/end).** (a) A generic-argument-list rule: `begin` = `<` immediately after a type-name character (`(?<=[A-Za-z0-9_])<`), `end` = `>`, `name` = `meta.generic.vilan`, delimiters `punctuation.definition.generic.begin/end.vilan`, patterns = itself + types + the binder rule — nesting gives `>>>` three ends. (b) The binder rule inside it: `\\b(type)\\b(?=\\s+(?:[A-Za-z_]|_))` → `keyword.other.type-binder.vilan` (or `storage.modifier.vilan` — pick the one the shipped themes colour as a keyword, and say which themes you checked); `_` there is `variable.language.wildcard.vilan` if the theme has a colour for it. (c) The element rule requires the `<` NOT to follow an identifier character (`(?<![A-Za-z0-9_])`) — element syntax's own atom-position rule (S2) already says a tag `<` starts an atom, so this is the grammar catching up with the spec, not a new rule; `<type` can never be a tag. (d) The terminator rule: scope only inside an element head — an element-head begin/end (from `<tag` to `>`/`/>`) is the honest form of E115's stopgap; if that is too large, the terminator rule at least excludes a `>` that closes a generic (the generic rule from (a) consumes it first when the list began on an earlier line — a begin/end spans lines, which is the whole point).

**Third place.** The book's highlight.js theme (`vilan/docs/theme/vilan.js`) is the grammar's twin for word lists (grammar_sync's GENERATION covers keywords/primitives/operators only); check whether it mis-colours the same head and fix the structural rule there too if so.

**Semantic layer.** If vilan-lsp classifies `type` binders or brackets, its class wins in VS Code — fix the classification there (E2's span classes) or leave those spans unclassified so TextMate paints them; report which layer owned each of the owner's three observations.

**Pins.** `grammar_sync` must stay green (the generated word-list fragments are byte-held: regenerate with `VILAN_REGENERATE_GRAMMARS=1` only if a generated fragment moved, and say so); a NEW scope-assertion test beside it that tokenises the exhibit with `vscode-textmate` under node (grammar_sync already reads the grammar with node) and asserts: every angle bracket in the head carries the generic delimiter scope, none carries the tag or operator scope; `type` carries the binder scope; `<div>` still tokenises as a tag (control); `a < b` still an operator (control).
